scope: Evidence-backed protocol and conduct obligations matched to study archetype and design tags. The catalog does not choose a universal best design or certify scientific validity.

obligations: Bind eligibility, assignment sequence, concealment, intervention/comparator, primary outcomes, stopping, SAP, harms, and participant flow to versions and execution receipts.
Separate planned blinding and intervention delivery from what was actually executed.
Resolve registration applicability from governing ethics, law, registry, funder, reporting, and venue requirements; do not infer it from the adapter alone.
transfer_limits: Bias associated with concealment/blinding varies by outcome type and setting.
Reporting completeness does not prove unbiased conduct.

obligations: Specify target population, strategies, eligibility, assignment, time zero, follow-up, estimand, confounders, missingness, and identification assumptions.
Keep emulation choices and sensitivity analyses versioned relative to outcome access.
Do not convert design emulation into proof that exchangeability, positivity, consistency, or measurement assumptions hold.
transfer_limits: Target-trial framing applies to causal questions, not every observational study.
Explicit design cannot eliminate unmeasured confounding.

obligations: Record source population, sampling/selection, variables, measurement timing, missingness, exclusions, model-selection status, and sensitivity analyses.
Distinguish exploratory associations from prospectively specified tests.
Keep causal language outside the allowed inference boundary unless identification is separately supported.
transfer_limits: STROBE is reporting guidance, not a design or quality certificate.
Many observational studies are appropriately exploratory or descriptive.

obligations: Bind data snapshots, unit/group/time split, preprocessing fit scope, labels, code/environment, seeds, hyperparameters, selection budget, and evaluation outputs.
Prevent train/test or group leakage and report benchmark changes or reused test feedback.
Separate executable reproduction from independent replication and scientific validity.
transfer_limits: Leakage depends on the scientific unit, prediction target, hierarchy, and deployment scenario.
Exact rerun does not prove generalization or absence of conceptual error.

obligations: Record experimental unit, species/strain/sex/age, allocation, randomization, blinding, sample-size rationale, exclusions, procedures, welfare, and adverse outcomes.
Distinguish unknown execution from not performed and from not applicable.
Account for cage, litter, batch, operator, and other hierarchical dependence when relevant.
transfer_limits: ARRIVE completion does not certify low risk of bias or ethical adequacy.
Species and laboratory context require domain-specific welfare and measurement standards.

obligations: Version the review question, eligibility, sources/platforms, exact searches, dates/limits, screening, extraction, risk-of-bias, synthesis, certainty, and update rule.
Preserve protocol amendments and exact executed search strings.
Do not equate PRISMA completion with an exhaustive or unbiased review.
transfer_limits: Reporting standards do not prove search completeness or synthesis validity.
Specialized review types require extensions and domain-specific sources.

obligations: Record methodological orientation, researcher position/reflexivity, context, sampling rationale, consent, data generation, coding/interpretation process, negative cases, and evidence excerpts.
Use saturation only when it fits the methodology and define how it was assessed.
Justify data adequacy from study-specific information power and analytic goals; do not force a universal interview count or preregistration gate.
transfer_limits: COREQ applies to interviews/focus groups and cannot govern all qualitative traditions.
Reflexivity and adequacy are substantive judgments, not checkbox certification.

obligations: Record unit, assignment/counterbalancing, blinding where applicable, outcomes, sample-size rationale, stopping, exclusions, manipulations, QC, and analysis status.
Separate prospectively specified tests from data-contingent exploration.
Expose researcher degrees of freedom rather than treating a significant result as protocol evidence.
transfer_limits: Some experiments cannot blind every role or randomize naturally occurring factors.
Prespecification improves interpretability but does not replace measurement validity.

obligations: Version inclusion, acquisition, consent/governance, identifiers, transformations, QC, known defects, access conditions, and lineage.
Make availability, reusability, and analytic reproducibility separate states.
Keep sensitive data governed rather than treating open release as universal.
transfer_limits: FAIR is not synonymous with open and does not certify data accuracy.
Resource-specific quality and consent standards still apply.

obligations: Label data-contingent analyses and outcomes as exploratory or post hoc.
Preserve exact timing, transformations, exclusions, negative/null observations, and the path by which hypotheses were generated.
Do not require universal preregistration, but do not present postdiction as prospective confirmation.
transfer_limits: Exploration is scientifically valuable when labeled honestly.
A later prospective replication may strengthen a confirmatory claim but cannot retroactively change timing.
